fleet.verification: Quota increase requests only available to business accounts; organization member must ask master account.
fleet.notes: Quota console shows default/applied/immediate-increase limits by resource. Eligible requests auto-approve; others need service-administrator review taking several days. No single starting numeric cap or scalar review time established.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.note: Standard VPC Server VM: Stop just stops the VM; block storage persists (persistent_disk), no state capture on stop/idle documented. Only scheduled snapshots exist for the separate NAS product ('set the automatic creation cycle'), which is a scheduled backup, not this feature.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can create an image of the current status for a server you're using.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Two mechanisms, both disk-only (no memory): 'My server image' of a server (new servers can be created from it, also 'replica server'), and Block Storage snapshots (full or incremental) via console/API: 'If you create a snapshot, you can store data in storage and create new storage on the desired server with the generated snapshot to restore the stored data.' (server-snapshot-create-vpc). On KVM g3, a snapshot of the default storage can become a server image (server-snapshot-serverimage-vpc). Bare metal cannot create server images.

egress_allowlist.quote: If the ACG outbound rule settings do not exist, the request packet sent from the server may be blocked.
egress_allowlist.note: ACG (stateful security group, per network interface) has outbound rules by protocol/IP-CIDR/port; user-created ACGs start with no rules. Network ACL (stateless, per subnet) adds inbound/outbound IP rules (vpc-nacl-vpc). No hostname/domain egress rules found.

egress_http_rules.quote: Access Control Group (ACG) is an IP/Port-based filtering firewall service that enables you to control and manage network access between servers.
egress_http_rules.note: ACG and Network ACL are L3/L4 only; no HTTP-level egress rules documented for servers.

ingress_rules.quote: Access Control Group (ACG) is an IP/Port-based filtering firewall service that enables you to control and manage network access between servers.
ingress_rules.note: ACG inbound rules (source IP/CIDR or ACG, protocol, port) plus subnet-level Network ACL; private subnets without public IP possible.

guest_firewall.quote: without needing to separately manage the existing firewalls (iptables, UFW, and Windows firewall)
guest_firewall.note: Full KVM (g3) / Xen (g1/g2) VM with root; the ACG page itself refers to the in-guest iptables/UFW firewalls as the alternative.

secret_proxy.quote: Secret Manager helps save and manage any important confidential information
secret_proxy.note: Secret Manager is a KMS-encrypted secret store that the application reads (with rotation via Cloud Functions); no credential-injecting egress proxy.

volume_attach.quote: You can add additional storage to a server on top of the default storage.
volume_attach.note: Block Storage: KVM g3 up to 20 extra volumes of up to 16 TB (CB1/CB2/FB1/FB2); Xen g1/g2 up to 15 of up to 2 TB (SSD/HDD). Zonal.

volume_shared.quote: If you create a NAS volume and mount it on the server, you can reliably share data across multiple servers.
volume_shared.note: NAS product: NFS (Linux) / CIFS (Windows) volumes up to 20 TB, read-write, mounted by multiple servers; separate billing. Object Storage also exists (not a mount).

isolation.quote: Korea VPC g3 servers run on KVM; g1/g2 legacy lines run on Xen.
isolation.note: Card's GPU L4 mode is explicitly labelled '(KVM)'; g3 High CPU line is KVM-based full-VM isolation. Derived from card data, not a single doc sentence.

image_oci.quote: You can create an image of the current status for a server you're using.
image_oci.note: not offered: custom boot images are NAVER Cloud 'server images' / block-storage snapshots (VM disk images), not Docker/OCI container images.

docker_inside.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
docker_inside.note: derived: full root-access KVM/Xen Linux VM; Docker installs and runs normally like on any VPS. Not itself a managed container product.

desktop.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (plain IaaS VM; no managed VNC/RDP desktop-streaming product).

browser.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

computer_use.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

anti_bot.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (generic IaaS VM, not a browser/scraping product).

captcha_solving.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: Access Control Group (ACG) is an IP/Port-based filtering firewall service that enables you to control and manage network access between servers.
egress_ip_type.note: Standard cloud-datacenter public/NAT IPs; no residential/mobile IP product for this VM line.

snapshot.quote: You can create an image of the current status for a server you're using.
snapshot.note: Disk-only: 'My server image' and Block Storage snapshots. No memory/process-state capture documented.

fork.quote: new servers can be created from it, also 'replica server'
fork.note: Cloning is via server image / replica server, disk-based (not a running clone).

fork_running.quote: You can create an image of the current status for a server you're using.
fork_running.note: Clones are new servers booted from a disk image/snapshot, not a live clone of a running instance's memory/process state.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: You can create an image of the current status for a server you're using.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Server images / Block Storage snapshots are disk-only; no memory capture, so clones cannot resume running processes.

pause_resume.quote: Stop just stops the VM; block storage persists
pause_resume.note: Stop/Start reduces compute billing (storage still billed) but does not preserve memory state (that's snapshot=fs, not mem).

wake_on_request.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; this is a self-serve always-billed-when-running VM, no auto-wake-on-inbound-request feature documented.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: no automatic idle-stop feature documented for VPC Server; stop is a manual/API user action.

live_resize.note: Server spec (vCPU/RAM) changes on NAVER Cloud VPC Server require stopping the server first; not a live/hot resize of a running instance.

agent_harnesses.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no coding-agent templates/preinstalls.

harness_api.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

own_agent_api.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; separate NAVER AI products (CLOVA) exist but are not part of this VM compute product.

mcp_server.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
mcp_server.note: not offered: no MCP server for controlling VPC Server instances found.

lang_python.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
lang_python.note: derived: full root Linux VM; standard OS images (Ubuntu/CentOS/Rocky) ship with or allow installing Python freely.

lang_node.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
lang_node.note: derived: full root Linux VM; Node.js installs freely, same as any VPS.

public_ipv4.quote: Access Control Group (ACG) is an IP/Port-based filtering firewall service that enables you to control and manage network access between servers.
public_ipv4.note: VPC Server instances can be assigned a Public IP resource (billed separately); ACG inbound rules operate on that public-facing address.

inbound_https.quote: Access Control Group (ACG) is an IP/Port-based filtering firewall service that enables you to control and manage network access between servers.
inbound_https.note: Users can open port 443 via ACG inbound rules and run their own HTTPS server; no managed HTTPS-URL gateway is bundled, but inbound HTTPS reachability is user-configurable.

static_egress_ip.quote: Access Control Group (ACG) is an IP/Port-based filtering firewall service that enables you to control and manage network access between servers.
static_egress_ip.note: derived: a server with an attached Public IP resource uses that same fixed IP for outbound traffic (no shared/rotating NAT egress documented for a single-NIC VPC server).

windows.quote: without needing to separately manage the existing firewalls (iptables, UFW, and Windows firewall)
windows.note: ACG documentation explicitly references the in-guest Windows firewall as an alternative, confirming Windows Server images are offered on VPC Server.

macos.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no macOS instance type documented for NAVER Cloud VPC Server.

self_host.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; NAVER Cloud Platform is a public multi-tenant hyperscaler, not self-hostable software.

byoc.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; this is a hyperscaler-run public cloud, not a BYOC-deployable managed product.

open_source.quote: Server is a service that lets you create and scale servers on the cloud.
open_source.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; NAVER Cloud Platform is proprietary hyperscaler infrastructure.

max_session_h.note: This is an ordinary self-serve hourly-billed VM (VPC Server); it runs until the user stops it, with no documented maximum session length.

arm64.quote: CPU type: Blank: Intel, a: AMD
arm64.note: The official server-spec-code table enumerates only two CPU type values (blank = Intel, 'a' = AMD) across all g1/g2/g3 server types; no ARM/Graviton-equivalent option is listed anywhere in the Server, GPU Server, or Bare Metal Server catalogs.

soc2.quote: SOC 1, 2, 3 인증 안전한 서비스 제공 및 운영을 위한 내부통제감사 [인증범위] 네이버 클라우드 플랫폼 ... 네이버클라우드㈜는 ... 서비스에 대한 안전성과 서비스 조직의 신뢰성을 검증받기 위해 SOC 2, 3 인증을 받았습니다.
soc2.note: Official certification page lists SOC 1/2/3 attestation with scope 'NAVER Cloud Platform'; SOC 2/3 reports (AICPA SSAE 18 based) are described as obtained, though SOC 1/2 report copies are restricted-distribution (SOC 3 is the public summary).

hipaa.quote: ISO / IEC · SOC · CSA STAR · PCIDSS · ISMS-P / ISMS · CSAP · MTCS · CBPR
hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The official compliance/certification page enumerates NAVER Cloud Platform's full certification list (ISO/IEC 27001 family, SOC 1/2/3, CSA STAR, PCI DSS, ISMS-P/ISMS, CSAP, MTCS, CBPR) and does not mention HIPAA/BAA anywhere; the product and its compliance program are oriented at Korea/APAC (CSAP, ISMS-P, CBPR) rather than US healthcare regulation.

sso.quote: using the SAML standard, you can use NAVER Cloud Platform with the Identity Provider (IdP) account used within your organization and set access permissions for each account... External IdP login: information on how to do SSO login into a NAVER Cloud Platform account with an external account... External IdP login supports the SAML protocol.
sso.note: Ncloud Single Sign-On lets customers federate into their NAVER Cloud Platform account via an external SAML IdP (with documented Okta, OneLogin, Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID, and AWS integration guides); NAVER Cloud login itself (for third-party apps) uses OAuth2/OIDC.

eu_data_residency.quote: Currently, g3 servers are supported only in the Korea, Singapore, and Japan Regions.
eu_data_residency.note: VPC Server spec/region docs list only Korea, Singapore, and Japan Regions repeatedly (server types, zones, availability); no Germany/EU region exists for this compute service, so there is no EU data residency option. The two JS-rendered en-product pages 404'd, but the docs page (already cited in the card) settles this directly and confirms the card's existing 'Residency' caveat.
